pr_title: feat: Add support for authentication to the sdk, and plug it in the admin

comments.body: `useEmailPassLogin` now calls `sdk.auth.login`, which goes through the js-sdk `Client.fetch` and rejects with `FetchError` (`packages/core/js-sdk/src/client.ts:48-49`, `status` set, no `isAxiosError`). The login page still decides on a wrong password with `isAxiosError(error)` followed by `error.response?.status === 401` (`packages/admin-next/dashboard/src/v2-routes/login/login.tsx:45-46`). `isAxiosError` only checks `error.isAxiosError` (`packages/admin-next/dashboard/src/lib/is-axios-error.ts:4`), so it is false for a FetchError. A 401 on bad credentials therefore skips the field errors (`invalidCredentials` on email/password) and shows the generic `errors.serverError` instead. This happens on every wrong-password attempt.

`normalizeRequest` now sets `credentials: "omit"` for every config that is not `auth.type === "session"`. Before this change fetch used the default `same-origin`, so same-origin requests carried cookies. Now a `new Medusa({ baseUrl })` client without `auth` (the default JWT mode) never sends cookies, even to its own origin. Any same-origin deployment that relies on the cookie set by `/auth/session` for an SDK client that does not use session mode will be logged out. The fix is to keep `same-origin` as the non-session default, or to add `omit` only for cross-origin requests.

`"module"` changed from `commonjs` to `ES2020`, so `tsc --build` (used by `build` and `prepublishOnly`) now emits ESM syntax into `dist/`. `packages/core/js-sdk/package.json:5` still sets `"main": "dist/index.js"` and has no `"type": "module"` or `exports` map. A Node consumer that loads the published package with `require` or plain CommonJS `import` will fail with a SyntaxError on `export`/`import` in `dist/index.js`. The workspace consumer (the Vite dashboard) is not affected by this.
